the fishermen in the study area perceived that the size of the catch has declined, the number of fishing grounds has reduced, and the number of fishers has increased.
the fishermen’s perceptions on shifting baseline are significantly affected by their generation and that the younger generation has a lower awareness on the issue than the other two generations.
the older generation of fishermen in Tanga perceive the current size of fish catch to have declined drastically, while the younger generation does not share this view.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the shifting baseline syndrome in coastal fishing communities of Tanga.
the perceptions of the coastal fishers on the current state of the coastal fishery resources of Tanga, Tanzania.
the perceptions of coastal fishers on the state and status of the coastal fishery resources and their fishing grounds in Tanga region, Tanzania.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the younger generations of fishermen in Tanga are not as aware of the current status of the fishery stock as their older generations.

the older generation of fishermen perceive that the fishery stock and the size of the current catch have declined significantly, while the middle-aged and younger generations perceive that there has been a significant decline in the size of catch, but not in the fishery stock.
the baseline for what is a ‘good’ fishery is shifting among the fishermen of Tanga, Tanzania.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for more studies on the shifting baseline syndrome in Tanzania.

the current state of the marine ecosystem in the study area has declined drastically, and that the younger fishermen are not aware of this decline, as they have not experienced the pristine state of the ecosystem.
the current generation of fishermen has a different baseline for the state of fishery resources from that of their parents and grandparents, which is a reflection of the shifting baseline syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the younger generation of fishers in Tanga, Northeastern Tanzania, are not aware of the past state of the coastal ecosystem.
the older fishermen are the most knowledgeable on the state of the fishery, as they are the ones with the most experience in the industry.
the baseline for what is considered ‘healthy’ is not fixed but rather shifts over time, as each generation has a different perspective on what is normal and healthy.
